body: I do. Sorry for mixing up the name! I've edited the issue now.

Messing about with my native code today, I think I discovered a destructor I wrote that could deadlock. Interesting that that could have potentially caused the Godot editor to immediately crash rather than just deadlock. So I tweaked various things and at times Godot refused to load my native library whatsoever, but randomly trying different build configurations I got it loading again. And now I have the same behaviour on Mac as on Linux: the editor only crashes if I recompile my native library.

I guess to really get info on this I'd need to compile Godot from source and run that in a debugger, but as I can kind of work now I probably won't get to doing that right away...
Hi @hhyyrylainen, does changing `reloadable` in the `.gdextension` file to `false`, does that solve it?

I tested just on Linux (as I'm not on my Mac right now), but it does look like changing that to `reloadable = false` does help. When testing previously I had forgotten that setting exists, so I had changed just the library compile definition to not be hot reloadable which means my earlier test was wrong. So it does look like changing that setting to false does help with the problem.

I didn't get a crash this time when testing on Linux but I got the parse errors after recompiling my library and going back into Godot (for example: `  ERROR: res://scenes/game_main.gd:125 - Parse Error: Cannot find member "CIRCLE" in base "GameSimulation".
`). And then when I set the reloadable property to false in the `.gdextension` file (I restarted Godot editor here to make sure it was in a clean state) it then makes it not cause that error. So yeah I think the trigger of the problem is related to the `reloadable` property.

It's probably something for us to discuss on the next GDExtension call, because I could imagine there could be a way that we could have some sort of hash/timestamp value that if the extension we need to reload hasn't changed, then on refocus there's no need to reload the library. So we'd only reload it if (a) the extension hasn't been loaded yet or (b) if the extension library and/or the .gdextension resource file were modified since the last time it was loaded.

There could be some odd corner cases I am not considering, so we need to evaluate the potential impact, if any.

Encountered this today on my project as well, which will make extensive use of GDExtension for performance intensive code. IMO this is a severe bug in godot for people working in C++, as it essentially requires an editor restart on each new extension compile, negating much of the benefit of rapid prototyping an editor like this is supposed to give.
